fix_summary: The frep.o/frep.i and each of its N FPU-sequenced instructions are scheduling boundaries (RISCVInstrInfo::isSchedulingBoundary -> isInFrepBody/isFrepSequenced; walks back across fallthrough layout predecessors counting only certainly-sequenced FP instructions; only in functions where the frep pass recorded an frep, bounded by the largest N). No FP instruction can enter or leave the repeated body; integer code between body instructions (not repeated by Snitch) stays schedulable within the gaps. Upstream technique: ARMBaseInstrInfo::isSchedulingBoundary keeps the Thumb-2 IT block together (ARMBaseInstrInfo.cpp:2084 @ llvmorg-20.1.8).
why_not_bundling: The frep pass runs pre-RA, where frep and body are often in different blocks (freploop.ll hwloop1: FREP_O in bb.1, body in bb.2), so a bundle cannot be formed there, and pre-RA bundles of vregs are unsafe for RA. A post-RA bundling pass (KCFI-style, addPreSched2 + UnpackMachineBundles) would add a line to O0-pipeline.ll/O3-pipeline.ll = a test change this role cannot make. If the owner wants the stronger guarantee against non-scheduler passes (see residual_risks), that is the follow-up and needs a pipeline-test regen.
rule8: Defect is pre-existing: fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 '[LLVM/PULP/SNITCH] Support for PULP and Snitch cores/platforms' introduced FREP_O and SNITCHFrepLoops (git -C /home/ubuntu/llvm-project log pulp/integer_SIMD_fix -SFREP_O). Exposure at 20: 9122c5235ec8 '[RISCV] Enable bidirectional scheduling and tracking register pressure (#115445)'. No XCV equivalent (no repeat-next-N instruction on upstream RISC-V); GAP9 GCC has no FREP (not applicable).

Plus a function from logs/20-F014-review/split.ll (frep.o ends one block, body starts the address-taken next block): CHECK: frep.o / CHECK-NEXT: .LBB{{.*}}: / CHECK-NEXT: fdiv.d / CHECK-NEXT: fmul.d / CHECK-NEXT: fadd.d. Generate with update_llc_test_checks.py. Also a function from logs/20-F014/rev3/fcvth.ll (Zfh conversion inside the body): CHECK that the three sequenced body instructions fdiv.d/fadd.d/fadd.h follow frep.o with only fcvt.* between them (CHECK-NOT: fsh between frep.o and fadd.h).
residual_risks: Non-scheduler passes can still edit an frep body (pre-existing): machine-cp (UseCopyInstr) could delete a copy-like body fsgnj/fmv.d; RISCVMakeCompressible (C/Zca only) inserts instructions; the -O0 fast register allocator spills inside the body. A post-RA bundle (B79) would cover the same-block cases but needs a pipeline-test regen.

Block placement (after both schedulers) is not constrained to keep the body block after the frep block; if it moved it, the frep would repeat the wrong code regardless of scheduling (not observed). Bundles cannot span blocks; only placing FREP_O in the body's block would fix it (changes fork test CHECK lines).
MaxFrepBody is not serialized to MIR: a MIR test containing FREP_O that runs the scheduler gets no protection (no such test exists; only SNITCHFrepLoops creates FREP_O and it sets the field).
Nested frep (never produced by SNITCHFrepLoops): the walk stops at the nearest frep, so an outer body after an inner frep would be under-protected.
other_errors_seen: FREP at -O0 is broken (pre-existing; README says frep needs >= -O1): the frep pass counts an instruction it later deletes (twochains/flat/nested in logs/20-F014/repro/body-indep.ll: 'frep.o a0, 3' for a 2-flop body) and RegAllocFast puts spill stores inside the body (base-O0.s: frep.o 3; fadd; fsd spill; fadd).

SNITCHFrepLoops produces invalid MIR: -verify-machineinstrs fails on body-indep.ll at every -O ('MBB has allocatable live-in, but isn't entry...' x12 for $f0_d/$f1_d/$f2_d), and PHIs keep an incoming edge from a block that is no longer a predecessor (freploop.ll hwloop1 after snitch-freploops).

SNITCHFrepLoops::isInvalidLoopOperation: condition 'RC != FPR64 || RC != FPR32' is always true, so any instruction with a vreg operand is accepted into a frep body; containsInvalidInstruction also skips COPYs from the count although they can become real fmv instructions.
revision: 4: addresses review 3 (REJECT on FP-to-FP conversions). isFrepSequenced now answers no for any opcode whose name contains CVT (fcvt.h.s/s.h, fcvt.h.d/d.h, fcvt.s.d/d.s, Xsmallfloat fcvt.*, vfcvt.*) and for any instruction whose FP register operands have different widths. Justification: GVSoC isa_riscv_gen.py and isa_smallfloats.py tag all FP-format conversions nseq (fcvt.h.d/d.h commented out = unmodelled); a TableGen JSON dump of this LLVM shows all 115 of the 159 nseq mnemonics that exist in LLVM have a GPR operand or CVT in the opcode name, so all are excluded. Earlier: rev 3 = FP-only count + MaxFrepBody gate; rev 2 = cross-block walk; rev 1 = boundary.
hardware_model: Snitch FREP repeats the next N FP-sequenced instructions; integer instructions and FP instructions touching integer registers (plus fcvt.s.d/fcvt.d.s in the model) run once and are not counted. Consequence: rev 1/2 headline reproducers (integer slli/add/sw inside the body: nested-lat2-snitch-tune.ll, split.ll) are NOT wrong results on Snitch; the real miscompile is an unrelated FP instruction entering the body (fpintr.ll).
frep_pass_N_consistency: NOT consistent with the hardware model (report only, separate backlog item): SNITCHFrepLoops::containsInvalidInstruction counts all loop instructions except PHI/COPY/loop branches/debug/IV users, including integer and nseq FP instructions, and isInvalidLoopOperation's FPR test (RC != FPR64 || RC != FPR32) is always true so integer work is accepted into the body. logs/20-F014/rev3/ncount.ll at llc -O2: body 'fadd.d; fcvt.w.d; xor' gets 'frep.o a1, 3' -> the sequencer repeats fadd.d and then 2 FP instructions after the loop; the loop's integer xor runs once instead of 64x. The scheduling-boundary check only uses N as an upper bound and still protects at least the real body.
